name: Saltmouth — The Unfiltered Taste Broadcast
creator: Originating node: Peculiar Osadebay-Strömberg fan cluster, the Gray Zone Tier 1, Ward Six
description: A viral BCI trend in which participants consumed extreme or unusual flavor combinations — fermented shellfish paste cut with synthetic citric acid, raw grain alcohol mixed with copper-laced tap water, charred bone marrow gelatin — and broadcast the unfiltered sensory experience live through open neural feed channels, refusing all compression or palatability filters. The challenge was explicitly framed as an act of anti-sanitization: the Saltmouth feed was raw, ugly, and involuntary-feeling, a direct rebuke to the curated synth-cuisine culture dominating Tier 3-4 food media. At its peak in 2208, over 340,000 simultaneous feed nodes were running Saltmouth broadcasts during a single Meridian evening.
medium: live open neural feed, uncompressed sensory broadcast
cultural_impact: Saltmouth forced a public reckoning with feed palatability standards — the invisible corporate filters that softened, sweetened, and smoothed all sensory content before it reached consumer BCIs — and briefly crashed two Axiom Network content moderation servers when mass unfiltered streams overwhelmed their normalization infrastructure. The phrase 'go saltmouth' entered Drift Tongue as shorthand for any unfiltered, ugly, deliberately unpleasant act of honesty.
controversy: HelixCorp's BCI Compliance Division issued a Tier 2 content warning classifying uncompressed sensory feeds as a potential 'neurological distress vector,' and attempted to mandate compression floors on all public broadcast nodes; the ruling was widely ignored in the Gray Zone and became a flashpoint in the broader BCI autonomy debate. Several participants reported genuine nausea-cascade events in co-present bystanders whose BCIs received ambient bleed from high-intensity Saltmouth streams.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 food journalist who initially dismissed Saltmouth as the Gray Zone shock-culture discovers that one specific broadcast — a single anonymous feed from Ward Six, 2208 — contains embedded data patterns that look deliberate, as if someone used the uncompressed sensory stream to hide a signal inside the noise.

A HelixCorp BCI compliance technician tasked with enforcing the compression floor mandate finds herself secretly running Saltmouth feeds after hours, drawn to the only content that feels real in a city of smoothed edges — until the feeds start showing her things that aren't flavor.

The original Saltmouth node cluster is being quietly acquired by a Tier 4 synth-cuisine brand that wants to relaunch the aesthetic as a premium 'raw authenticity' product tier, and the Ward Six community that created it is organizing to destroy every archived feed before the brand can file intellectual property claims.
